## Claims
- [computed] For \(J=[333,5^5]\), \(Q=J/A_+J\) has free ranks \(1,1,2,2,2,1,1\) in degrees \(9,\ldots,15\), vanishes thereafter through degree \(25\), and has no torsion. [artifact b5658ec18b84ad470751544a752f238dadd447fb7b1122a89a299a79e024042f]
- [source-backed] The lower-adjoined Schur family \(\{\bar s_\mu: i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\) minimally generates \(J_v\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 220-235]
- [proved] **Basis criterion.** If homogeneous generators \(F\) generate \(J\), and \(Q=J/A_+J\) is torsion-free with \(\operatorname{rank}Q_d=\#F_d\) for every \(d\), then the images of \(F_d\) are a \(\mathbb Z\)-basis of \(Q_d\). Indeed, they give a surjection \(\mathbb Z^{\#F_d}\twoheadrightarrow Q_d\) between free groups of equal rank, hence an isomorphism.
- [proved] For the computed case \(i=j=b=3,\ a=2\), the criterion explains the accepted data: the generator enumerator is \(z^9\binom52_z\), so \(\operatorname{Hilb}_Q(z)=z^9\binom52_z\).
- [proved] Minimality alone cannot imply the basis criterion: for \(A=\mathbb Z[x]\), \(J=(2x,x^2)\), the two generators are minimal, but \(J/A_+J\cong\mathbb Z\{2x\}\oplus(\mathbb Z/2)\{x^2\}\).

## Strategy
Use the indecomposables basis criterion, rather than further Pieri/SNF computation. The accepted finite ranks and torsion-freeness verify its hypotheses only for \([333,5^5]\).

## Gaps
The requested general inference from minimality to a torsion-free indecomposables basis is not established; the displayed microcase refutes it. The original finite Hilbert-series target remains established only for its computed input.
